name: Client Data Retention & Deletion Scheduler

parameters.content:
## Client Data Retention & Deletion Scheduler

### How it works

1. The workflow starts by daily checking for newly closed client matters in Clio and applying retention policies to schedule data retention tasks.
2. It logs retention schedules into a Google Sheets ledger for tracking and compliance purposes.
3. On a daily basis, it reads the retention ledger to identify matters needing retention deadline reminders and sends color-coded reminder emails with action links.
4. It handles webhook requests when decisions are made on retention reminders, validating and updating the retention ledger accordingly.
5. The system responds appropriately to invalid requests or missing matter records, ensuring smooth interaction and compliance tracking.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure Clio API credentials and base URL as environment variables in the workflow.
- [ ] Set up Google Sheets credentials and access to the retention ledger spreadsheet.
- [ ] Configure email sending credentials (SMTP or email service) for sending retention reminder emails.
- [ ] Deploy and configure the webhook URL for handling retention decision callbacks.
- [ ] Adjust schedule triggers as needed for daily checks and reminders.

### Customization

Retention policy logic in the 'Check If Retention Needs Scheduling' code node can be updated to reflect firm-specific retention requirements. Email reminder content and escalation tiers can be customized in respective code nodes.

## Schedule closed matters check

Nodes triggered daily to fetch firm users and closed matters from Clio, split and filter them by close date, and schedule retention if needed.

## Daily retention reminder process

Nodes triggered daily to read retention ledger, filter and compute escalation tiers, build and log retention reminder emails, and send them out.

## Retention decision webhook handler

Nodes handling webhook triggers when a retention decision is made via emailed links, parsing requests and validating them.

## Invalid decision response

Responds with an invalid link page for webhook requests that fail validation.

## Retention ledger read for decision

Reads the retention ledger to find and process the retention decision corresponding to the matter id.

## Respond matter not found

Responds with a not found page if the matter id is missing in the retention ledger.

## Update ledger and confirm decision

Updates the retention ledger with the decision and responds with a confirmation page to the requester.

nodes.name: When Checking For Closed Matters Daily
nodes.notes: Fires every day at 6am (n8n server timezone) — adjust the cron expression if a different time suits your firm.

nodes.name: Fetch Firm Users From Clio API
nodes.notes:
Fetches the firm's user directory — used to resolve each newly closed matter's responsible attorney to a real name and email before logging it to the ledger, so the reminder branch never needs to re-look this up. A disabled/departed user (enabled: false) is treated as unresolved.

Runs first in this linear chain, feeding straight into the closed-matters fetch next — a genuine sequential dependency, not a disconnected side-fetch (confirmed live in PAC-63/64 that a disconnected side-fetch referenced only by name in code isn't reliably executed by n8n).

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as PAC-18/20/55/57/58/59/61/63/64/65/66/67 — reuse it if already deployed.

nodes.name: Fetch Closed Matters From Clio API
nodes.notes:
Fetches every matter Clio currently shows as Closed. Every run re-fetches the full closed-matter list (not just recently changed ones) since the dedupe that prevents duplicate ledger entries happens downstream, keyed by matter id, in workflow static data — this is simpler and safer than trying to detect 'newly' closed via a date filter, at the cost of re-fetching matters this workflow has already scheduled on every run (harmless, just extra API calls).

Confirmed live: 'close_date' and 'practice_area{id,name}' both read correctly. A real matter with no practice area or responsible attorney set in Clio correctly returns null for those fields, rather than erroring -- 'Check If Retention Needs Scheduling' downstream already falls back gracefully (DEFAULT_RETENTION_YEARS, blank attorney fields) when that happens.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as the user directory fetch above.

nodes.name: Split Out Closed Matter Records
nodes.notes: Turns the single API response into one n8n item per closed matter. An empty or missing 'data' array (e.g. after a Clio error, or genuinely no closed matters) simply produces zero items.

nodes.name: Filter Closed Matters With Close Date
nodes.notes: Drops any closed matter with no close date set — a retention deadline can't be computed without one, and that gap itself is worth the firm noticing on its own (e.g. by fixing the matter's dates directly in Clio).

nodes.name: Calculate Retention Scheduling Needs
nodes.notes: The RETENTION_POLICY_YEARS map is the entire policy surface of this template — the one thing every firm must customize before going live. Static data is local to this n8n instance's execution store; fine for the single-instance deployment this template targets.

nodes.name: Filter Matters Needing Retention
nodes.notes: Keeps only matters this workflow has never scheduled before. On most days this drops to zero, which is normal, not a failure — most closed matters were already scheduled on a prior run.

nodes.name: Append Retention Schedule To Sheet
nodes.notes:
Appends one row per newly closed matter — the permanent audit record of when each matter's data is due for retention review, and (once decided) what happened and when.

Create the 'Retention' tab with EXACTLY these column headers in row 1, in any order, before running this live — the append matches by column NAME, so a missing header means that field silently has nowhere to land (confirmed live: a sheet missing 'status'/'last_action'/'last_action_at' caused every ledger row to come back with an empty status, which made Branch B's 'Filter Ledger Entries Still Scheduled' drop every row and never alert on anything):

matter_id, matter_ref, matter_description, practice_area, client_name, close_date, retention_years_applied, retention_deadline, attorney_name, attorney_email, status, last_action, last_action_at.

RETENTION_LEDGER_SHEET_ID is the Google Sheet's ID (the long string in its URL between /d/ and /edit).

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → Google Sheets OAuth2 → sign in with the account that owns this sheet.

nodes.name: When Sending Retention Reminders Daily
nodes.notes: Fires every day at 7am (n8n server timezone) — completely independent of the scheduling branch above; it doesn't share any state with it except the same Google Sheet, read fresh every run.

nodes.name: Read Retention Ledger From Sheet
nodes.notes:
Reads every row ever logged to the ledger, returning one n8n item per row. Confirmed live: Google Sheets returns date columns back as the exact plain-text string they were written as (e.g. '2033-08-27'), not reformatted — the date parsing downstream works as written.

Credential: same Google Sheets OAuth2 credential as the scheduling branch above.

nodes.name: Filter Scheduled Retention Ledger Entries
nodes.notes: Only rows still in status 'scheduled' can ever alert — once an attorney confirms deletion or places a legal hold, this drops it from every future reminder run automatically. 'Extend' keeps a row in 'scheduled' with a pushed-out deadline, so it keeps being tracked.

nodes.name: Calculate Retention Escalation Tier
nodes.notes: Static data is local to this n8n instance's execution store — fine for the single-instance deployment this template targets; flag it if the firm later scales to a multi-worker n8n setup.

nodes.name: Filter Entries Needing Alert Today
nodes.notes: Drops any ledger entry more than 90 days out, or already alerted for its current tier. On most days this drops to zero, which is normal, not a failure.

nodes.name: Build Retention Reminder Email Content
nodes.notes: Explicitly set to 'Run Once for Each Item' — more than one matter reaching a tier on the same day is entirely plausible and must not be silently dropped (same real bug already found and fixed elsewhere in this catalog, PAC-63/65's build-email steps).

nodes.name: Execute Compliance Audit Logging
nodes.notes:
Logs the reminder to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet via the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) — internal record-keeping only, not a client message. Its 'approved'/opt-out result is deliberately ignored: this is an internal firm safety net, same fire-and-forget pattern used for internal-only notifications elsewhere in this catalog (PAC-59/60/61/63/67).

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable. This REPLACES $json with the guardrail's own response, so 'Send Retention Reminder Email' reaches back to 'Build Retention Reminder Email' by name for every field it needs.

nodes.name: Send Retention Reminder Email
nodes.notes:
Delivers the reminder to the responsible attorney (or FIRM_EMAIL if unresolved). Reads every field explicitly from 'Build Retention Reminder Email' by name rather than $json, since the guardrail call immediately upstream replaced the item's json with its own response.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

nodes.name: When Retention Decision Received Webhook
nodes.notes:
Receives the click-through from one of the reminder email's three action links (GET request, matter_id and action as query parameters). Copy this node's Production URL into the RETENTION_DECISION_WEBHOOK_URL n8n Variable once, after activating this workflow.

A generic form/link webhook, not a Clio API webhook — no OAuth scope, no verification handshake, no expiring subscription to maintain (unlike PAC-66's Clio-webhook design).

nodes.name: Parse Retention Decision Request Data
nodes.notes: is_valid_request is false if there's no matter_id, or the action isn't exactly one of confirm/extend/hold — guards against a malformed or tampered link.

nodes.name: If Retention Decision Request Valid
nodes.notes:
Yes (usable matter_id and a recognized action) → look it up in the ledger.
No (malformed or tampered link) → show an error page without touching the ledger.

nodes.name: Respond With Invalid Link Page
nodes.notes: Shown when the click-through link itself is malformed — same plain-HTML confirmation-page pattern as PAC-55's dismiss link.

parameters.responseBody:
⚠️
Something looks off
This link is missing information or has expired. Nothing was changed. Please open the retention ledger directly to record a decision.

nodes.name: Read Retention Ledger For Decision
nodes.notes:
Reads every ledger row so the next step can find the one matching this decision's matter_id — same 'read everything, filter in code' approach as the reminder branch, avoiding any dependency on Google Sheets' own row-filter syntax.

Credential: same Google Sheets OAuth2 credential as the rest of this workflow.

nodes.name: Compute Retention Ledger Update
nodes.notes: found is false if the matter_id in the link doesn't match any ledger row (e.g. the row was deleted, or the link is stale) — routes to a distinct error page rather than silently writing a new row.

nodes.name: If Retention Matter Found In Ledger
nodes.notes:
Yes (matching row found) → update the ledger and show the confirmation page.
No (no ledger row matches this matter_id) → show a distinct 'not found' page without writing anything.

nodes.name: Respond With Matter Not Found Page
nodes.notes: Shown when the link's matter_id doesn't match any current ledger row.

parameters.responseBody:
⚠️
Matter not found
This matter no longer appears in the retention ledger. Nothing was changed. Please check the ledger directly.

nodes.name: Update Retention Ledger With Decision
nodes.notes:
Updates the matching row (matched on matter_id) with the new status, retention date, and decision timestamp. This is the ONLY write this branch performs — it updates a spreadsheet row, never a Clio record, and never deletes any client data or file.

Credential: same Google Sheets OAuth2 credential as the rest of this workflow.

nodes.name: Respond With Decision Confirmation Page
nodes.notes: Shows the attorney a plain confirmation of exactly what was recorded — reads action_label back from 'Find Matching Row And Compute Update' by name, since the Sheets update immediately upstream replaced $json with its own response. Same confirmation-page pattern as PAC-55/62.

main.node: Fetch Closed Matters From Clio API
If Retention Matter Found In Ledger
Filter Closed Matters With Close Date
Respond With Matter Not Found Page
Fetch Firm Users From Clio API

description: Runs on three independent triggers. Daily: fetches every Clio matter with status Closed, applies the firm's own retention policy by practice area, and logs a new row to a Google Sheets ledger with the computed retention date -- but only once per matter, ever. Daily (separate): re-reads the ledger and escalates at 90/30/7 days before each retention date, plus a continuous daily alert once overdue, giving the responsible attorney one-click Confirm/Extend/Hold actions. Webhook: records whichever decision was clicked. This workflow never deletes client data under any circumstance -- 'confirm' only records authorization; the actual deletion always remains a manual, human-executed step in Clio and any document management system (ABA Op. 512). Replaces manual retention tracking and legal-hold spreadsheets.
